S.B. Criminal Revision Petition No. 1085/2002 Bhagwan Singh Alias Dharmi son of Shri Nanga, by caste Jat,
resident of village Samra, Police Station Fatehpur Sikri, Distt.
Agra (UP).

(Presently confined in Distt. Jail at Bharatpur)
 ----Petitioner  Versus State  ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr.S.K.Gupta with Ms.Surabhi  Agarwal For Respondent(s) : Mr.Ramesh Choudhary, PP  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE FARJAND ALI  Judgment / Order 08/12/2021

The instant revision petition is directed against the judgment dated 25.10.2002 passed by learned Addl. Sessions Judge, Fast Track No.3, Bharatpur in criminal appeal no. 58/2002 (33/2000)
whereby he affirmed the judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bharatpur in criminal regular case no. 236/1987 vide order dated 29.9.2000 whereby the petitioner has been convicted under Section 7 r/w 16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act read with Sec. 50(1)(15) of Bhagwan Singh Alias Dharmi vs State on 8 December, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195485454/
1 PF Act and sentenced him to suffer six months rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.1,000/- and in default of payment of fine to further undergo two months simple imprisonment.

sentences.text:
[CRLR-1085/2002]
 Learned counsel for the petitioner though challenged the legality, correctness and propriety of the judgment passed by the courts below, however, at the outset submits that instead of arguing the matter on merit or challenging the conviction, the part of the sentence may be modified to the extent of sentence he has served on the ground that the matter pertains to year 1986 and it was his first offence and has faced the rigour of trial and legal proceedings for 35 years.
He submits that the petitioner is a poor milk man and on examination, the seized milk was not found spurious but found adulterated.
He submits that the accused has remained in custody in this case for 09 days and now the petitioner has become very old and, therefore, a lenient view may be taken against him.
Learned Public Prosecutor has opposed the prayer made by counsel for the petitioner.
Heard, perused the material available on record.

In the totality of facts & circumstances of the case,
considering the fact that the incident took place in the year 1986 for having adulterated milk which has not been found spurious in laboratory though adulterated and the fact that the accused has Bhagwan Singh Alias Dharmi vs State on 8 December, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195485454/
2 faced rigour of trial and proceedings for long 35 years and now he has become very old person and it is his first case, his antecedents are not such so as to dis-entitle him for reduction of sentence, I deem it just and appropriate that sentence awarded by the learned trial court and affirmed by the learned Appellate Court deserves to be reduced to the period already undergone by him while maintaining the conviction.
(3 of 3) [CRLR-1085/2002

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ] Accordingly, the revision petition is partly allowed.
The conviction of the petitioner for the offences under Section 7/16 and 50(1)(15) of PF Act, 1954 is maintained.
However, the sentence is reduced to the period already undergone by him.
The bail bonds furnished by the petitioner are hereby discharged.

(FARJAND ALI),J SANDEEP RAWAT /23/62 Powered by TCPDF (www.tcpdf.org)
